open_points.subject: M21 StoredValue disclosure_class with authored trial data (M06 add trial case action)
open_points.text: "The class of a value is set by exactly one rule: a flow input's value takes its flow input port's class ... a flow constant's value takes the class the composing agent declares with it; a function's output takes the highest class its execution received; a binding's output takes the class the binding declares (K-14)."
open_points.question: When an agent adds an authored TrialCase, who sets disclosure_class for TrialCase.inputs and authored expected_outputs, and what validation rule applies?
options: Agent supplies the class per value, kernel validates it against the contract input port's accepted maximum
Kernel derives input classes from contract ports and derives expected output class from the case's highest input class
All authored trial values are forced to one fixed class (for example `open`)
open_points.default_guess: Agent supplies input classes (validated <= accepted max); expected output class is derived by kernel from the case's highest input class.

open_points.subject: M06 TrialCase.expected_outputs coverage
open_points.text: "expected_outputs: StoredValues by output port, absent when only the absence of failure is required"
open_points.question: If expected_outputs is present, must it include every output port of the contract version, or can it assert only a subset of outputs?
options: May include a subset; only listed ports are checked for equality
Mode flag distinguishes full-output vs subset assertion
open_points.default_guess: Require all output ports when expected_outputs is present.

open_points.subject: M23 NodeExecution.executed for owner refusal
open_points.text: "executed: the implementation or the binding, absent for `skipped_by_guard` and `upstream_failed`, which record a node that was not executed;" together with status including `refused_by_owner`
open_points.question: For status `refused_by_owner` (effect not sent because owner refused), is `executed` present (binding referenced) or absent (node treated as not executed)?
options: Present: keep binding in `executed` even though send did not occur
Absent: treat refusal as a non-executed node like other skipped cases
open_points.default_guess: Present with the binding reference, plus failure detail that owner refused before send.
